title: Can you send it to me?
grammar: Object pronouns (me / you / him / her / it / us / them)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender os pronomes objeto me, you, him, her, it, us e them para falar de pessoas e coisas sem repetir o nome. No dia a dia do escritório da Delta Ducon, você pede favores, encaminha e-mails e passa recados o tempo todo — e esses pronomes deixam suas frases mais curtas e naturais.
intro: At the office, we do not repeat every name. We say: Can you send it to me? Please call him. The manager needs them today.
Today we practise object pronouns. They come after the verb or after a small word like to, for or with, and they make your English at Delta Ducon quick and clear.
introAudio: Good morning. Today we learn object pronouns. Can you send it to me? Please help her with the report. The team needs us in the meeting room. Let us practise them together.
vocab: I work with him; he is a good colleague.
Can you give her this message?
Can you do me a favour, please?
The client is on the phone; please answer it.
The manager needs us in the meeting.
I have the file; I can send it to you.
practice: My ______ is on holiday, so I answer his emails.
colleague
Please give her this ______ from the client.
message
Can you do me a ______ and print this contract?
favour
The client is on line one; please take the ______.
call
The manager wants the whole ______ in room two.
team
I have the ______ here; I can email it to you.
file
Send the ______ to me and I will read it now.
file
He is a new ______, so please help him this week.
colleague

audio.title: A quick favour
audio.text: Hi, this is Ana from reception. The director needs the report, so can you send it to me now? I will print it and give it to him before the meeting. The client called this morning; I did not answer her, but I have her number here. Can you call her back for us? The team is waiting for the documents, so please email them today. Thank you very much for helping me.

readAloud: Can you send it to me, please?
The manager needs us in the meeting room.
Please give her this message from the client.
I have the report; I can email it to you.
The new colleague is here; please help him.
fill: The director wants the report; please send it to ___ . (I)
Ana is busy, so I answer the phone for ___ . (she)
Carlos is new here; please show ___ the office. (he)
The team is waiting; the client needs ___ now. (we)
Here is the file; can you email ___ to the client? (the file)
The visitors are late, so we cannot start without ___ . (they)
I sent you the agenda; did you receive ___ ? (the agenda)
Thank you for helping ___ with the report today. (I)
qa: Can you send the file to me?
Yes, I can send it to you now.
Do you know the new colleague?
Yes, I work with him every day.
Where is the manager?
She is in her office; please call her.
Does the team need the documents?
Yes, please email them to us today.
Did you get the message?
Yes, thank you, I received it this morning.

a.label: Can you ... it to me?
a.placeholder: Can you send it to me, please?

b.label: help him / her / them
b.placeholder: Please help her with the report.

sentences: Can you send it to me, please?
The director needs the report; please give it to him.
The client called; can you call her back?
The team is waiting for us in the meeting room.
Here is the file; I can email it to you.
The visitors are late; we cannot start without them.
My colleague is busy, so I help him today.
Thank you for sending the agenda to us.
grammarPoint: Object pronouns substituem o objeto da frase (a pessoa ou coisa que recebe a ação): me, you, him, her, it, us, them. Eles vêm depois do verbo ou depois de to, for, with. Please call him. — Por favor, ligue para ele. Can you send it to me? — Você pode enviar isso para mim?
deepDive: Cuidado para não confundir os pronomes sujeito (I, he, she, we, they) com os objeto (me, him, her, us, them). O sujeito faz a ação; o objeto recebe. Certo: She helps me. (Ela me ajuda.) Errado: She helps I. Para coisas usamos sempre it, e para o plural, them. Depois de with, for e to, também use a forma objeto: with us, for them, to her.
examples: Please send it to me.
Por favor, envie isso para mim.
I can help you with the report.
Eu posso ajudar você com o relatório.
The manager needs him at the meeting.
O gerente precisa dele na reunião.
Can you call her this afternoon?
Você pode ligar para ela hoje à tarde?
The client wants it by Friday.
O cliente quer isso até sexta-feira.
The team is waiting for us.
A equipe está esperando por nós.
Please email the files to them.
Por favor, envie os arquivos para eles por e-mail.
Thank you for helping me today.
Obrigado por me ajudar hoje.
mistakes: Depois de to usamos me, não I.
O objeto de he é him.
O objeto de she é her.
Depois de for usamos us, não we.
I email the files to they.
I email the files to them.
O objeto de they é them.
quick: The client wants to speak to ___ . (he)
Can you help ___ with the agenda? (she)
The manager needs ___ in the meeting. (we)

celebrate.en: Well done. With object pronouns your emails and messages sound natural — short, polite and clear for the whole team.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Com os pronomes objeto seus e-mails e recados soam naturais — curtos, educados e claros para toda a equipe.

title: Is this yours or mine?
grammar: Possessive pronouns (mine / yours / his / hers / ours / theirs)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender os pronomes possessivos mine, yours, his, hers, ours e theirs para dizer de quem é algo sem repetir a palavra. No escritório da Delta Ducon há muitos objetos e documentos parecidos — canetas, mesas, pastas, relatórios — e esses pronomes ajudam você a esclarecer o que é de cada um.
intro: In a busy office, things get mixed up. Is this pen yours or mine? This desk is hers, and that one is his. The blue folder is ours.
Today we practise possessive pronouns. They tell us who owns something without repeating the noun, so your English at Delta Ducon stays short and clear.
introAudio: Good morning. Is this cup yours or mine? This desk is hers, and that one is his. The meeting room is ours today. Today we learn possessive pronouns. Let us practise them.
vocab: This pen is not mine; it is yours.
That desk near the window is hers.
The blue mug is his, not mine.
This laptop is ours; the office bought it.
The corner office is his now.
practice: Is this ______ on the table yours or mine?
pen
The ______ near the window is hers.
desk
The blue ______ with coffee is his.
mug
This ______ is ours; the company bought it last year.
laptop
The ______ by the gate is theirs, not ours.
parking space
The corner ______ on the second floor is his now.
office
That ______ is not mine; ask your colleague if it is his.
pen
Please do not use that ______; it is hers.
desk

audio.title: Whose is this?
audio.text: Every Monday the office is a little messy. Is this pen mine or yours? The blue mug on my desk is not mine; I think it is his. The red folder is ours, but the grey one is theirs. That laptop is hers, so please do not use it. My desk is the one near the window, and yours is next to the door. The parking space by the gate is theirs now, and this new one is ours. Let us keep our things in the right place.

readAloud: Is this pen yours or mine?
The desk near the window is hers.
This laptop is ours; the company bought it.
The blue folder is his, not mine.
That parking space is theirs now.
fill: This pen is not mine; I think it is ___ . (you)
The mug on the desk is ___ , not mine. (he)
That laptop near the window is ___ . (she)
The meeting room is ___ until noon. (we)
The blue folder is not ___ ; ask the other team. (we)
Those parking spaces by the gate are ___ . (they)
This desk is ___ ; you sit here every day. (you)
The red mug is ___ ; I use it every morning. (I)
qa: Is this pen yours?
No, it is not mine; I think it is yours.
Whose desk is near the window?
That desk is hers.
Is this laptop his?
Yes, it is his; please do not use it.
Is the meeting room ours today?
Yes, it is ours until noon.
Whose is that parking space?
It is theirs; ours is by the gate.
sentences: This pen is mine, not yours.
The desk near the window is hers.
That laptop is his; please do not use it.
The meeting room is ours until noon.
The grey folder is theirs, and the red one is ours.
Is this mug yours or mine?
The corner office is his now.
That parking space by the gate is theirs.
grammarPoint: Possessive pronouns dizem de quem é algo sem repetir o substantivo: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. Não vêm antes de um substantivo (isso é o adjetivo: my, your). This is my pen. → This pen is mine. — Esta caneta é minha. Is this yours? — Isto é seu?
deepDive: Não confunda o adjetivo possessivo (my, your, his, her, our, their + substantivo) com o pronome possessivo (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs, que ficam sozinhos). Certo: This is my desk. / This desk is mine. Errado: This is mine desk. Atenção: hers, ours, yours e theirs NÃO levam apóstrofo — nunca escreva her's ou their's. E cuidado: its (dele/dela para coisas) não é usado como pronome possessivo isolado.
examples: This pen is mine.
Esta caneta é minha.
Is this folder yours?
Esta pasta é sua?
The blue mug is his.
A caneca azul é dele.
That desk is hers.
Aquela mesa é dela.
The meeting room is ours today.
A sala de reunião é nossa hoje.
Those parking spaces are theirs.
Aquelas vagas são deles.
Your desk is here, and mine is over there.
Sua mesa é aqui, e a minha é ali.
This laptop is not mine; it is hers.
Este notebook não é meu; é dela.
mistakes: Antes do substantivo usa-se my, não mine.
O pronome possessivo é hers, não her.
O pronome possessivo é ours, não our.
quick: This pen is ___ ; I bought it. (I)

celebrate.en: Great job. Now you can say whose things and files are whose — a small skill that keeps any office tidy and friendly.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo trabalho. Agora você sabe dizer de quem são as coisas e os arquivos — uma pequena habilidade que mantém qualquer escritório organizado e amigável.

title: What do you like doing at work?
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a falar de preferências no trabalho usando like, love, don't like e hate seguidos do verbo com -ing. No dia a dia da Delta Ducon você vai contar o que gosta e o que não gosta de fazer — desde responder e-mails até participar de reuniões — de um jeito simples e educado.
intro: Everyone has favourite tasks and boring ones. I like answering emails, I love meeting clients, but I don't like filing papers.
Today we practise like, love, don't like and hate with the -ing form of the verb. This is how you talk about your preferences at work in natural English.
introAudio: Good morning. What do you like doing at work? I love talking to clients, and I like organising the agenda. I don't like filing papers, and I hate waiting for slow emails. Today we practise like, love and hate plus -ing. Let us begin.
vocab: I like answering emails in the morning.
I don't like filing old documents.
I hate waiting for a slow reply.
practice: I like ______ before the first meeting.
answering emails
The director loves ______ new clients in person.
meeting
I don't like ______ old contracts all afternoon.
filing
She loves ______ the agenda for the whole week.
organising
We hate ______ for a slow answer from a supplier.
waiting
The team likes ______ new colleagues at Delta Ducon.
training
He doesn't like ______ for the meeting to start.
waiting
I love ______ the manager's agenda every Monday.
organising

audio.title: My favourite tasks
audio.text: I am an assistant at Delta Ducon, and I have my favourite tasks. I love answering emails in the morning, because the office is quiet. I like organising the agenda and booking the meeting rooms. I don't like filing old documents, but it is part of the job. I really hate waiting for slow replies from suppliers. My favourite part of the week is training new colleagues, because I enjoy helping people. What do you like doing at work?

readAloud: I like answering emails in the morning.
The director loves meeting new clients.
I don't like filing old documents.
We hate waiting for slow replies.
She loves organising the agenda.
fill: The director loves ___ clients in person. (meet)
She loves ___ the agenda every Monday. (organise)
We hate ___ for a slow reply. (wait)
I don't like ___ the phone during lunch. (answer)
qa: What do you like doing at work?
I like answering emails in the morning.
Do you like filing documents?
No, I don't like filing documents.
What does the director love?
He loves meeting new clients.
Do you hate waiting for replies?
Yes, I hate waiting for slow replies.
What does the team enjoy?
The team likes training new colleagues.
sentences: I like answering emails in the morning.
The director loves meeting new clients.
I don't like filing old documents.
She loves organising the agenda every week.
We hate waiting for slow replies from suppliers.
The team likes training new colleagues.
He doesn't like working late on Fridays.
I love booking the meeting rooms for the week.
grammarPoint: Depois de like, love, don't like e hate, usamos o verbo com -ing para falar de preferências. I like answering emails. — Eu gosto de responder e-mails. She hates waiting. — Ela odeia esperar. Repare que em português usamos 'de' (gosto DE responder), mas em inglês não há preposição: apenas verbo + -ing.
deepDive: A ordem de intensidade é: love (adoro) > like (gosto) > don't like (não gosto) > hate (odeio). Na terceira pessoa (he, she), o verbo principal ganha -s: She likes, He loves, She doesn't like. Cuidado com a grafia do -ing: make → making (tira o -e), organise → organising, sit → sitting (dobra a consoante). Erro comum: NÃO diga 'I like to answering'; ou 'I like answering' ou 'I like to answer' — mas não misture os dois.
examples: I like answering emails.
Eu gosto de responder e-mails.
She loves meeting clients.
Ela adora encontrar clientes.
We don't like filing papers.
Nós não gostamos de arquivar papéis.
He hates waiting for replies.
Ele odeia esperar por respostas.
They love organising the office.
Eles adoram organizar o escritório.
I don't like working late.
Eu não gosto de trabalhar até tarde.
The manager likes training new staff.
O gerente gosta de treinar novos funcionários.
Do you like booking flights?
Você gosta de reservar voos?
mistakes: Depois de like usamos o verbo com -ing.
Com she o verbo like ganha -s.
Não misture to com -ing; escolha um.
Com he usamos doesn't, não don't.
Depois de hate usa-se -ing, sem to.
quick: I like ___ emails in the morning. (answer)

celebrate.en: Excellent. Now you can share what you enjoy and what you don't at work — a friendly, human way to connect with your team.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Agora você consegue dizer do que gosta e do que não gosta no trabalho — um jeito amigável e humano de se conectar com a equipe.

title: Let's have a meeting
grammar: Sugestões — Let's / Shall we / Why don't we / How about + -ing
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a fazer sugestões educadas no trabalho com Let's, Shall we?, Why don't we? e How about + -ing. Nas reuniões e conversas do dia a dia da Delta Ducon, sugerir ideias com gentileza ajuda a organizar tarefas, marcar horários e trabalhar bem em equipe.
intro: Good teamwork needs good suggestions. Let's start the meeting. Shall we book room two? Why don't we call the client together? How about sending the report today?
Today we practise four polite ways to make a suggestion. They help you propose ideas at Delta Ducon in a friendly, professional way.
introAudio: Good morning. Let's practise suggestions today. Shall we start the meeting? Why don't we call the client together? How about booking room two for two o'clock? These are polite ways to share an idea at work. Let us begin.
vocab: That is a good suggestion for the agenda.
Let's take a short break at ten.
Shall we reschedule the meeting to Friday?
Why don't we check the agenda first?
How about booking the small room?
practice: That is a great ______ for the next meeting.
suggestion
Let's take a short ______ after the call.
break
Shall we ______ the meeting to Friday morning?
reschedule
Why don't we check the ______ before we start?
agenda
How about booking the small ______ for two o'clock?
room
Let's finish the report ______ this afternoon.
together
The client is busy today; shall we ______ the call?
reschedule
Everyone is tired; let's have a ______ now.
break

audio.title: Planning the meeting
audio.text: The team has a lot to do this week, so let's plan the meeting. Shall we start at nine on Tuesday? Why don't we invite the sales team too? How about booking the big room on the second floor? Let's send the agenda by email today, so everyone is ready. The client is very busy this week; shall we reschedule the call to Friday? Good, let's do it. How about taking a short break after the first hour? That is a great suggestion.

readAloud: Let's start the meeting at nine.
Shall we book the big room?
Why don't we call the client together?
How about sending the agenda today?
Let's take a short break after the call.
fill: Let's ___ the meeting at nine o'clock. (start)
How about ___ the agenda by email? (send)
Why don't we ___ the client together? (call)
Shall we ___ the small room for two? (book)
How about ___ a short break now? (take)
Let's ___ the report together this afternoon. (finish)
How about ___ the meeting to Friday? (move)
Why don't we ___ the sales team too? (invite)
qa: Shall we start the meeting now?
Yes, let's start. Everyone is here.
How about booking the big room?
Good idea. Let's book it for two o'clock.
Why don't we call the client together?
Yes, that is a good suggestion.
Shall we reschedule the call to Friday?
Yes, let's reschedule it to Friday morning.
How about taking a short break?
Great idea. Let's take ten minutes.

a.label: Let's ...
a.placeholder: Let's start the meeting at nine.

b.label: How about ...-ing?
b.placeholder: How about booking the small room?

sentences: Let's start the meeting at nine.
Shall we book the big room?
Why don't we call the client together?
How about sending the agenda today?
Let's take a short break after the call.
Shall we reschedule the meeting to Friday?
Why don't we invite the sales team?
How about finishing the report this afternoon?
grammarPoint: Quatro formas educadas de sugerir. Let's + verbo base: Let's start. — Vamos começar. Shall we + verbo base? Shall we start? — Vamos começar? Why don't we + verbo base? Why don't we call? — Por que não ligamos? How about + verbo com -ing? How about calling? — Que tal ligar? Repare: só How about pede o verbo com -ing; as outras três usam a forma base.
deepDive: Let's é a contração de Let us e é a forma mais direta e amigável de sugerir algo que vocês farão juntos. Shall we...? é um pouco mais formal e pede resposta. How about...? também pode vir seguido de um substantivo: How about a coffee? (Que tal um café?) ou How about Friday? (Que tal sexta?). Cuidado: NÃO diga 'How about to book'; é sempre How about booking (verbo + -ing) ou How about + substantivo.
examples: Let's start the meeting.
Vamos começar a reunião.
Shall we book the room?
Reservamos a sala?
Why don't we call the client?
Por que não ligamos para o cliente?
How about sending the report today?
Que tal enviar o relatório hoje?
Let's take a short break.
Vamos fazer uma pausa curta.
Shall we reschedule the call?
Remarcamos a ligação?
Why don't we invite the sales team?
Por que não convidamos a equipe de vendas?
How about meeting at ten?
Que tal nos encontrarmos às dez?
mistakes: Depois de Let's usa-se o verbo base, sem to.
How about to book the room?
Depois de How about usa-se o verbo com -ing.
Depois de Shall we usa-se o verbo base.
Why don't we to call the client?
Why don't we call the client?
Depois de Why don't we usa-se o verbo base.
Depois de Let's o verbo fica na base, sem -s.
quick: Shall we ___ the room for two? (book)

celebrate.en: Well done. Polite suggestions make you a great team player — now you can share ideas in meetings with confidence.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Sugestões educadas fazem de você um ótimo colega de equipe — agora você compartilha ideias nas reuniões com confiança.

title: Where is the report?
grammar: Preposições de lugar (in / on / under / next to / between / behind)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender as preposições de lugar in, on, under, next to, between e behind para dizer onde as coisas estão. No escritório da Delta Ducon você localiza documentos, arquivos e objetos o tempo todo — e essas palavrinhas ajudam você a explicar exatamente onde cada coisa está.
intro: Where is the report? It is on the desk. The pen is in the drawer, and the box is under the table.
Today we practise prepositions of place. They tell people exactly where things are, so nothing gets lost at the Delta Ducon office.
introAudio: Good morning. Where is the report? It is on the desk, next to the laptop. The folder is in the drawer, and the box is under the table. The printer is behind the door. Today we learn prepositions of place. Let us begin.
vocab: The pen is in the top drawer.
The files are on the shelf.
The printer is behind the door.
The contracts are in the metal cabinet.
The laptop is on the desk.
The meeting room is next to the corridor.
practice: The signed contract is in the top ______.
drawer
The old files are on the top ______.
shelf
The ______ is behind the door, near the window.
printer
The client folders are in the grey ______.
cabinet
The laptop is on the ______, next to the phone.
desk
The meeting room is next to the main ______.
corridor
Please put the report on my ______ before lunch.
desk
The paper is in the ______ under the printer.
drawer

audio.title: Finding the documents
audio.text: Good morning. Let me help you find the documents. The signed contract is on the desk, next to the laptop. The client folders are in the grey cabinet, behind the door. The extra paper is in the top drawer, under the printer. The old reports are on the shelf, between the two boxes. The meeting room is next to the corridor, on the second floor. If you cannot find something, ask me and I will show you where it is.

readAloud: The report is on the desk.
The pen is in the drawer.
The box is under the table.
The printer is behind the door.
The folder is between the two boxes.
fill: The report is ___ the desk, next to the phone. (on / in)
The pen is ___ the top drawer. (in / on)
The box of paper is ___ the table. (under / on)
The printer is ___ the door, near the window. (behind / in)
The small folder is ___ the laptop, on the left. (next to / in)
The grey file is ___ the two boxes on the shelf. (between / on)
The contracts are ___ the metal cabinet. (in / on)
The chair is ___ the desk, ready for the visitor. (next to / under)
qa: Where is the report?
It is on the desk, next to the laptop.
Where are the client folders?
They are in the grey cabinet.
Where is the printer?
It is behind the door, near the window.
Where is the extra paper?
It is in the top drawer, under the printer.
Where is the meeting room?
It is next to the corridor, on the second floor.

b.label: next to / between / behind
b.placeholder: The folder is between the two boxes.

sentences: The report is on the desk.
The pen is in the top drawer.
The box of paper is under the table.
The printer is behind the door.
The laptop is next to the phone.
The grey file is between the two boxes.
The client folders are in the metal cabinet.
The meeting room is next to the corridor.
grammarPoint: Prepositions of place dizem onde algo está. on = sobre uma superfície (on the desk). in = dentro de algo fechado (in the drawer). under = embaixo (under the table). next to = ao lado de (next to the phone). between = entre duas coisas (between the boxes). behind = atrás de (behind the door). The report is on the desk. — O relatório está sobre a mesa.
deepDive: Cuidado com on x in: usamos on para superfícies (on the table, on the shelf, on the wall) e in para espaços fechados (in the drawer, in the cabinet, in the room). between é sempre usado com DUAS coisas (between A and B); para três ou mais, use among. next to significa 'ao lado de' e é o mesmo que beside. Lembre: para responder 'onde?', comece com It is... ou They are... seguido da preposição.
examples: The report is on the desk.
O relatório está sobre a mesa.
The pen is in the drawer.
A caneta está na gaveta.
The box is under the table.
A caixa está embaixo da mesa.
The phone is next to the laptop.
O telefone está ao lado do notebook.
The file is between the two boxes.
O arquivo está entre as duas caixas.
The printer is behind the door.
A impressora está atrás da porta.
The folders are in the cabinet.
As pastas estão no armário.
The chair is next to the desk.
A cadeira está ao lado da mesa.
mistakes: The report is in the desk.
The report is on the desk.
Sobre uma superfície usamos on, não in.
The pen is on the drawer.
The pen is in the drawer.
Dentro de algo fechado usamos in.
The box is behind of the door.
The box is behind the door.
The file is between the boxes and the shelf and the wall.
The file is between the two boxes.
between é usado com duas coisas.
The phone is next the laptop.
The phone is next to the laptop.
A expressão correta é next to.
quick: The printer is ___ the door. (at the back)
The file is ___ the two boxes. (in the middle)

celebrate.en: Fantastic. Now you can say exactly where everything is — a simple skill that saves the whole office time every day.
celebrate.pt: Fantástico. Agora você sabe dizer exatamente onde cada coisa está — uma habilidade simples que economiza tempo de todo o escritório todos os dias.
